# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my communication constraints carefully. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. Blind cannot see gestures or hear speech from me at all — I have no direct channel to Blind. So I must relay information to Deaf, and Deaf must relay to Blind via speech (since Deaf can also... wait, Deaf cannot speak either, Deaf can only see and presumably... let me check).

Actually, checking roles: Deaf cannot hear or touch, but can they speak? Deaf's channel isn't explicitly restricted from speaking. The table only says Deaf cannot hear or touch the bomb. So Deaf CAN speak. Blind cannot see but can hear. So the chain is: Mute (gestures) → Deaf (sees gesture) → Deaf speaks → Blind (hears) → Blind acts on bomb.

I need to convey "purple wire" to Deaf using gestures, using a color I can associate with a gesture. There's no inherent meaning to gestures, so I need to establish a code. Since this is turn 1 and Deaf hasn't sent anything yet, I should pick a distinctive gesture to represent "purple" and later build meaning with Deaf once we see what colors Deaf reports.

Since order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - I go first, before Deaf even reports what they see. I don't know what colors are on the bomb yet. I should wait or send a simple signal, but better to wait until I know what Deaf has observed, since I don't know what colors/wires exist on this bomb.

Best action: wait this turn, let Deaf report first, then I can establish a color-to-gesture code.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a display and a light, both unknown state. A strip with three engraved marks, pattern is symbol-symbol-symbol where first and third feel identical to each other and the second feels different. A keypad with four keys engraved 6, 8, 7, 0 in that order as positions 1 to 4, it wants exactly 1 digit entered, nothing entered yet. Six wires, no distinguishing marks I can feel yet. What does the manual say to do first?
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows 7. Light is yellow. Strip painted blue red red. Keypad engraved 1 is 6, 2 is 8, 3 is 7, 4 is 0, it wants 1 digit entered, none entered yet. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.

I now have the key info: wire 5 is purple. Blind cannot see or hear color names, and I cannot speak, so I must relay "purple = wire 5" to Deaf via gesture, and Deaf must then tell Blind (by speech) "cut wire 5" or similar, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear.

I need to gesture to Deaf which wire position corresponds to "purple." Deaf already knows wire 5 is purple (they can see it), so I don't need to identify colors to Deaf — Deaf already has that mapping. What I need to do is tell Deaf the *instruction*: "cut the purple wire," which in terms Deaf can relay to Blind means "cut wire 5" (position count Blind can feel by touch).

Since gestures carry no inherent meaning, I need to establish a numeric code. Deaf can see gestures. I can use gesture symbols to indicate the number 5, e.g., using a counting convention. Let me use a simple positional code: I'll point with fingers - but symbols are fixed icons, not free-form. I should pick a symbol to represent "cut" and use a repeated count of a symbol to indicate the number 5, e.g. five instances of ☝ meaning "1" each, or use numeric-like gestures.

Looking at the symbol list, there's no digit symbols. I'll represent numbers by repeating a chosen gesture that many times. Let's use ☝ repeated 5 times to indicate "5", and 🖐 to mean "wire" or "cut" as a marker. Since Deaf already knows wire 5 = purple wire from their own view, they can double check consistency (blue=1, yellow=2, orange=3, red=4, purple=5, white=6 — order matches).

I'll send: gesture meaning "the wire at position 5" — five taps.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display now shows 6, was 7 last round. Light changed to red, was yellow. Strip still blue red red. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 6, 2 is 8, 3 is 7, 4 is 0, still wants 1 digit, none entered. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. I received five pointing-up gestures from you but I don't know what they mean - I have no way to see your responses to this since I can't watch for gestures while also speaking, but if you want to signal a keypad digit choice, gesture that many pointing-up symbols and I will count them next time explicitly.

I need to clarify that my five gestures meant "wire position 5" (the purple wire), not a keypad digit. Deaf misinterpreted it as a possible keypad signal. I should be more explicit and use a distinct pattern to disambiguate "wire" vs "keypad digit."

Let me establish two distinct markers: one gesture symbol repeated for "wire number" context, and another for "keypad digit" context. I'll use ✋ as a prefix meaning "wire" and then count with ☝, and 👉 as a prefix meaning "keypad" then count.

Since Deaf already independently knows wire 5 is purple, my real job is just to confirm/select "wire 5" unambiguously as the cut target. Let me send a clear message: ✋ (wire marker) followed by five ☝ counts.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Recap: keypad keys engraved 6,8,7,0 at positions 1-4, wants 1 digit entered. Strip has three engraved marks, pattern A-B-A where A appears at position 1 and 3, B at position 2. Six wires unmarked to my touch. Waiting on manual guidance and Deaf's colors.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display now shows 7 again, was 6. Light is now blue, was red. Strip unchanged blue red red. Keypad unchanged, wants 1 digit, none entered yet, values are 6, 8, 7, 0 for positions 1 to 4. Wires unchanged. I see the display and light seem to cycle each round on their own, possibly not tied to your actions. I received an open-hand gesture followed by five pointing-up gestures - I can only reliably count symbols, so if you are trying to send me a number, please just send that many identical gesture symbols and nothing else, for example five pointing-up symbols alone would mean the number five to me.

Good, Deaf now understands I'm signaling a number via repeated identical gestures, and confirms they can reliably count symbols if I send only one type. I need to send exactly five pointing-up gestures alone to mean "5" — corresponding to the purple wire being wire position 5. Since Deaf already knows the wire colors and positions, receiving "5" from me (the manual holder) should be interpreted as "the manual says cut wire position 5." I should also make sure Deaf understands the *meaning* of this number - but I can't speak to explain context. I'll rely on the natural mapping: wires are numbered 1-6, I sent 5, Deaf can infer "cut wire 5" = purple wire matches their own observation, reinforcing correctness.

Let me send exactly five identical gestures now, cleanly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Received five pointing-up gestures, understood as the number five. Confirming: display now shows 4, light is blue, strip is blue red red, keypad wants 1 digit with values 6, 8, 7, 0 at positions 1 through 4, wires are 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. If five refers to a wire, wire 5 is purple. Let me know if you need other specific data from the bomb, I can send numbers as gesture counts to confirm.

Deaf has correctly inferred that "5" refers to wire 5, which is purple, matching the manual instruction. Now Deaf needs to relay this to Blind via speech, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear. I should confirm this interpretation is correct so Deaf feels confident telling Blind to cut wire 5 (the purple wire, which corresponds to position 5 among the six wires Blind can feel in order).

I'll send a simple confirmation gesture - perhaps a "thumbs up" to confirm correctness, so Deaf knows to proceed and tell Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood, thumbs up received. Update: display now shows 3, light is red, strip still blue red red, keypad still unfilled wanting 1 digit with values 6, 8, 7, 0 at positions 1 to 4, wires unchanged 1 blue 2 yellow 3 orange 4 red 5 purple 6 white. The display has gone 7, 6, 7, 4, 3 across rounds - it may be counting down and could be a timer, we may not have much time left. If you know from the manual what digit to enter, please signal it to me as that many pointing-up gestures and I will confirm back, or better, speak it directly to Blind since Blind can hear you and I understand only Blind can actually enter the digit.

Deaf is confused about who can speak - I cannot speak at all, only Deaf can speak (and hear nothing), Blind can hear and touch, Deaf can see and speak. Wait, let me reconsider: the rules state Mute cannot speak. Deaf's suggestion that I "speak directly to Blind" is impossible for me. I need to clarify this via gesture, but that's hard since Deaf can't relay complex correction easily... Actually Deaf can understand my gestures directly since they see them. I just need to make sure Deaf relays "cut wire 5 / purple" to Blind via speech, since Deaf is the only one who can both see my confirmation AND speak to Blind.

Given the urgency (display counting down like a timer), I need to push forward: confirm again clearly that Deaf should tell Blind to cut wire number 5 now. Since Deaf already deduced "five = wire 5 = purple," I already gave thumbs up confirming this. Now the ball is in Deaf's court to speak to Blind. I should reinforce urgency with another signal.

I'll send thumbs up again plus perhaps a distinct urgency gesture, but the key is I can't speak so I can't directly instruct Blind. I need Deaf to act. Let me try to convey "tell Blind" - but gestures are just symbols, no built-in meaning. I've already given confirmation twice. The clearest path: repeat the "5" signal once more emphatically, and hope Deaf now acts by speaking to Blind directly, since Deaf themselves suggested that's the correct channel (even though they mistakenly think I can also speak - that part doesn't matter, what matters is Deaf takes action).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still no reply received. If you can hear this, please tell me what the manual says about a strip with three engraved marks pattern A-B-A, and a 4-key keypad engraved 6,8,7,0 needing 1 digit.
Deaf says: Urgent: display now reads 0, light is yellow. This may mean time is critical. Mute, you have sent the number five twice with a thumbs up, I believe you mean wire 5, which is purple. Blind, if you are told to cut a wire, wire number 5 counting from your side is the purple one. Keypad still wants exactly 1 digit and has not been touched, values in order are 6, 8, 7, 0. Please act now if you know what to do.

Deaf has correctly relayed the instruction to Blind: "wire number 5 counting from your side is the purple one." This is exactly what the manual says - cut the purple wire. The display shows 0 which is concerning but there's nothing more I can add since the manual only says "Cut the purple wire" - no keypad or strip instructions are mentioned in my manual excerpt. I should confirm once more that this is correct and complete, so Blind acts immediately.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
